Article Title: Parliament winter session likely in 1st week of December; delimitation bill to be in focus
Article Text:
The government faces a numbers test as it seeks opposition support for the proposed constitutional amendment

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The winter session of Parliament is likely to commence in the first week of December, news agency PTI reported on Sunday. The government is looking to secure passage of a Constitution amendment bill linking women's reservation to delimitation. This comes as opposition parties prepare to intensify their protests over the special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The proposed legislation seeks to increase the strength of the Lok Sabha from 543 to a maximum of 850 seats through delimitation, enabling the implementation of 33% reservation for women in Parliament and state legislatures before the 2029 Lok Sabha elections.The possible dates are being discussed at the highest levels of the government, PTI reported citing sources.However, the bill faces a significant numbers challenge. A Constitution amendment requires the support of at least two-thirds of members present and voting. In the current Lok Sabha, this translates to 361 votes if all 540 members vote, with three seats vacant.The ruling NDA has 320 members and will need opposition support to cross the required threshold. A senior government functionary, however, expressed confidence on Thursday that the legislation would clear Parliament by a margin of 15 to 18 votes.The legislative push is also likely to coincide with a fresh confrontation between the government and opposition over the SIR exercise. Opposition parties have stepped up their criticism of the electoral roll revision and are demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Their protests could spill into the winter session and disrupt parliamentary proceedings.An MP from the ruling alliance said a Constitution amendment bill could not be debated and put to vote unless the House functioned in an orderly manner.Meanwhile, the government's decision not to prorogue the Monsoon session has added to speculation about the next parliamentary sitting. The session was adjourned sine die on August 13 but has remained unprorogued for 94 days, exceeding the previous record of 87 days in 2008.Keeping the session alive has allowed the government to retain the option of convening an extended sitting at short notice. Such a sitting would require a minimum notice of two days, compared with at least 14 days for convening a fresh session.The government is also learnt to be considering a formula to address concerns over the proposed delimitation, particularly those raised by southern states. Under the proposal being explored, Lok Sabha seats could be increased by 50% across states while retaining their existing inter-state share based on the 1971 Census. No final decision has been taken on the framework.The proposed constitutional amendment had failed to secure the required numbers during a special sitting of Parliament on April 17.
Article Summary: The winter session of Parliament is likely to commence in the first week of December. The government is looking to secure passage of a Constitution amendment bill. This comes as opposition parties prepare to intensify their protests over the special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

Article Title: IndiGo Guwahati-bound flight returns safely to Pune after landing gear fails to retract
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: An IndiGo Airbus A320 (VT-IZE) operating from Pune to Guwahati on Sunday had to return to the origin after its landing gear did not retract after take off. The aircraft with about 200 people on board had taken off at 7.17 am and the pilots discovered they were unable to retract the gear which made it impossible to proceed on the journey. Deciding to return, they contacted Pune air traffic control. As per protocol, the Pune airport, which is an Indian Air Force base, made all emergency preparations for its landing which the aircraft safely did just after 9 am. Flight movement timings are as per Flightradar 24 data.Tanked up for the about three-hour flight, the pilots first flew the aircraft in a hold for about an hour near Pune to burn fuel and get within maximum landing weight. Once there, they then did a low pass over the Pune runway so that air traffic control could visually verify the position of the landing gear gear to confirm to the cockpit that the same is indeed out and that is okay to land. This is done as per protocol to rule out a false indication of landing gear position in the flight deck.An IndiGo spokesperson said: “6E 623 of Nov 15 returned to origin and landed safely at the Pune International Airport after a technical snag was detected shortly after take-off.In line with standard operating procedures, all relevant authorities were immediately informed. The aircraft is undergoing maintenance checks and will resume operations after securing necessary clearances.”“An alternate aircraft has been arranged promptly to operate the flight. We regret the inconvenience caused to our customers and are taking all possible measures to minimise it, including offering them regular updates, meals and refreshments, alternate flight options and refunds, as applicable. We thank our customers for their patience and understanding. At IndiGo, the safety and comfort of our customers and crew remain our top priority,” the spokesperson added.A flight with landing gear out returns to the origin as continuing the journey will mean increased drag that leads to a much higher fuel burn of about 150%.
Article Summary: An IndiGo Airbus A320 (VT-IZE) operating from Pune to Guwahati had to return to the origin after its landing gear did not retract after take off. The aircraft with about 200 people on board had taken off at 7.17 am and the pilots discovered they were unable to retract the gear.

NEW DELHI: Pakistan announced on Saturday that it will participate in the inaugural Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue, scheduled to be held in New Delhi from November 20 to 22. Prime Minister Narendra Modi had proposed the dialogue at the SCO summit in Tianjin in 2025.The last visit by a Pakistani minister to India was in May 2023, when then Foreign Minister Bilawal Bhutto Zardari travelled to Goa to attend a meeting of SCO foreign ministers. This will also be the first ministerial visit between the two countries since the Pahalgam terror attack last year.Pakistan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs said that Musadik Masood Malik, Federal Minister for Climate Change and Environmental Coordination, will lead the country’s delegation to the dialogue.India had invited culture minister Aurangzeb Khichi for the event. Musadik Masood Malik, federal minister for climate change and environmental coordination, will lead the team. He however, is considered a more experienced minister in the Pakistan govt. "The event will bring together representatives from SCO member states to exchange views on issues related to civilisational dialogue and cultural understanding," said Pakistan in its announcement, adding that Islamabad remains committed to promoting dialogue among civilisations and fostering people-to-people ties within the SCO framework in a spirit of mutual respect.After Bilawal's visit in 2023, external affairs minister S Jaishankar had visited Pakistan the next year, again for a meeting of SCO foreign ministers. On both occasions, there was no bilateral meeting between the ministers.Even in the absence of any substantive bilateral engagement for over a decade, both countries have continued to interact within the Eurasian bloc which they both joined as full members in 2017.Pakistan currently holds the SCO presidency and will host the heads of state summit next year. In the current circumstances, Modi's participation in it is unlikely as India's position - that talks and terror can't go hand in hand - has hardened further after the Pahalgam attack.
Article Summary: Pakistan announced on Saturday that it will participate in the inaugural Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue. Prime Minister Narendra Modi had proposed the dialogue at the SCO summit in Tianjin in 2025. This will also be the first ministerial visit between the two countries since the Pahalgam terror attack last year.

Article Title: 'Introspect on your own prejudices': India hits back at US religious freedom panel over Sharjeel Imam post
Article Text:
Kwatra's remarks came after US commission described jailed activist Sharjeel Imam as a person detained in India for his religious freedom advocacy.

NEW DELHI: India's ambassador to US, Vinay Mohan Kwatra on Saturday hit back at the US Commission on International Religious Freedom (USCIRF), saying it had "no locus standi" to comment on the constitutional rights of Indian citizens.His remarks came after the commission described jailed activist Sharjeel Imam as a person detained in India for his religious freedom advocacy.In a strongly worded post on X, Kwatra rejected the commission's assessment and accused it of making partisan and ill-informed remarks about India's commitment to religious freedom and equal rights."USCRIF has no locus standi to sit in judgment over the constitutional rights of Indian citizens. Its habitual partisan, ill-informed, and jaundiced assessments cannot diminish India’s constitutional commitment to religious freedom and equal rights for all faiths," Kwatra said."India flourishes defying the agenda-driven partisan narratives of the USCIRF. Taking the same liberty that USCIRF so readily assumes, a word of advice: introspect on your own prejudices and stop lecturing others," he added.USCIRF shared Imam's profile on X, describing him as "a Muslim man detained in India for his religious freedom advocacy".The commission's post linked his detention to his advocacy for religious freedom, prompting a sharp response from the Indian envoy.Imam, a former student activist was arrested in January 2020 in connection with protests against the Citizenship Amendment Act (CAA) held in December 2019 and January 2020, according to ANI. Authorities accused him of delivering speeches that allegedly incited communal violence.In August 2020, he was charged in connection with FIR 59/2020, which relates to the alleged larger conspiracy behind the February 2020 North-East Delhi riots, according to ANI.The case, being investigated by the Delhi Police Special Cell, invokes provisions of the Indian Penal Code and the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA). The charges include rioting, murder, promoting enmity, unlawful activities and alleged terrorist acts.Imam was earlier granted interim bail from October 4 to October 10 to attend his cousin's wedding functions. The relief came with conditions barring him from using social media, interacting with media persons or meeting anyone other than family members, relatives and friends.Established by the US government in 1998 after the inaction of the International Religious Freedom Act, the recommendations of USCIRF are non-binding on the US State Department.
Article Summary: India's ambassador to US, Vinay Mohan Kwatra hit back at the US Commission on International Religious Freedom (USCIRF) His remarks came after the commission described jailed activist Sharjeel Imam as a person detained in India for his religious freedom advocacy. Kwatra accused the commission of making partisan and ill-informed remarks about India's commitment to religious freedom and equal rights.

Article Title: From odd-even to cloud seeding: Why Delhi's pollution battle remains unfinished
Article Text:
National Capital witnesses health emergency

2024 vs 2026: What changed in strategy?

Rules under AAP

Rules under BJP

Why Delhi keeps choking

Prolonged exposure to toxic air

Seasonal firefighting or lasting solutions

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Every winter, Delhi's air turns toxic.Governments change, action plans get revamped and new solutions are announced.Yet, the capital continues to battle hazardous air, with residents bearing the health costs of a crisis that refuses to go away.At the time of publishing this article on Saturday (7pm IST), Delhi's average Air Quality Index (AQI) stood at 367, in the ‘very poor’ category, which had breached the ‘severe’ level on Friday.The latest spike came days after Delhi recorded its most polluted Diwali in five years.Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) and Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) governments introduced separate action plans and announced a range of measures to tackle Delhi's recurring air pollution crisis during their respective tenures. Both failed.So are successive governments fighting pollution at its source, or merely trying to manage the smog after it sets in?When AAP was in power in Delhi, its 2024 Winter Action Plan focused on a combination of emergency interventions, dust suppression and monitoring of pollution sources.The 21-point plan, announced in September 2024, included drone surveillance of pollution hotspots, a special task force, anti-dust campaigns at construction sites and the deployment of mechanical road sweepers, water sprinklers and mobile anti-smog guns.The odd-even vehicle scheme was another emergency option used by AAP govt to reduce vehicular emissions if air quality deteriorated further.The AAP government's plan also targeted industrial pollution, open waste burning and stubble burning. It called for stricter monitoring of construction sites, action against polluting industrial units and enforcement of pollution-control norms.A ban on firecrackers was announced ahead of Diwali to prevent a seasonal spike in emissions.Following BJP's victory in the February 2025 assembly elections, the new government under chief minister Rekha Gupta introduced a 25-point Air Pollution Mitigation Plan in June, followed by a separate Winter Action Plan in October 2026.Its strategy placed greater emphasis on enforcement against polluting vehicles, construction dust and industrial emissions. Measures included ANPR cameras to identify overage vehicles, restrictions on certain polluting commercial vehicles, expansion of electric public transport and stricter checks at PUC centres. For dust control, the government announced the deployment of 86 mechanical road sweepers, 300 water sprinklers and 362 anti-smog guns under its winter plan.BJP also attempted cloud seeding in October 2025 as an experimental measure to induce artificial rain and wash pollutants out of the air. However, the two trials conducted on October 28 failed to produce rainfall, with insufficient moisture in the clouds cited as the primary reason.A subsequent trial was also called off because of unfavourable atmospheric conditions.This year, the Supreme Court permitted the use of certified green firecrackers during Diwali under limited hours.While emergency interventions such as cloud seeding, smog guns and traffic restrictions are often discussed as possible solutions, environmental experts argue that the problem requires a more sustained, science-led approach. Sunil Dahiya, founder and lead analyst at EnviroCatalysts, explains why these measures have limited impact and what Delhi needs to address the pollution crisis in the long run.Dahiya said cloud seeding cannot be a reliable solution to Delhi's winter pollution as it requires moisture-laden clouds, which are largely absent during the smog season."You can't seed clouds that aren't there," he said, adding that even if artificial rain is induced, the relief may last only a few hours. Pollution also moves across administrative boundaries and can quickly return due to emissions from the wider Delhi-NCR airshed. "Cloud seeding treats the symptom, at best, for a few hours," he said.On the contribution of vehicles to Delhi's pollution, Dahiya said they remain among the biggest local sources of PM2.5. Citing IITM's real-time data, he said vehicular emissions accounted for 31% of PM2.5 on November 13, making them the largest single direct source. However, he cautioned against relying solely on restrictions without improving public transport."You can't ban your way out if people have no alternative," he said, pointing out that around 6,400 buses with GPS were tracked on Delhi's roads on November 13, below the city's long-standing target.He also questioned the effectiveness of smog guns and water sprinklers in reducing city-wide PM2.5 levels, saying they mainly settle coarse dust over limited areas, while winter pollution is largely driven by fine combustion particles and secondary pollutants.Calling for dust control through paving, covering construction materials and mechanised sweeping, he described spraying water into the air as "visible action, not effective action".The impact of Delhi's recurring pollution crisis goes beyond seasonal coughing, breathlessness and respiratory infections. Doctors warn that prolonged exposure to polluted air can affect lung development in children and increase the risk of respiratory and cardiovascular problems.Dr Nikhil Rajvanshi, Consultant – Pediatric Pulmonologist, Allergy and Sleep Specialist, Rainbow Children's Hospital, Delhi, explains that children inhale more air relative to their body weight than adults, making them particularly vulnerable to pollutants. He warns that children exposed to high pollution levels over several years may experience reduced lung growth and lower lung function as adults. Importantly, even children without diagnosed respiratory conditions are not immune. "Some effects may persist even after exposure decreases," he cautions.Highlighting the wider health implications, Dr Vikas Mittal, Director – Pulmonology, CK Birla Hospital, Delhi, says PM2.5 particles can penetrate deep into the lungs and enter the bloodstream, triggering inflammation across the body. Repeated exposure can worsen asthma and COPD, impair lung function and increase cardiovascular risks, including hypertension, heart attacks and strokes. He also warns that prolonged exposure can cause lasting changes to lung tissue, even among otherwise healthy individuals."Some changes may improve when exposure is reduced, but prolonged injury and remodelling of lung tissue may not be completely reversible," he says.The doctors also highlight the potential consequences of continued exposure over the next five to ten years. Dr Rajvanshi warns that an entire generation of children growing up in highly polluted environments could face reduced peak lung function, increased asthma prevalence and greater susceptibility to respiratory infections in adulthood.Dr Mittal cautions that the consequences would not be limited to people with existing illnesses, as otherwise healthy individuals are also vulnerable to the cumulative effects of prolonged exposure.With the crisis extending beyond Delhi's borders, responsibility cannot rest with one government or one agency alone. It requires coordination between the Centre, Delhi and neighbouring states, along with measurable targets and accountability for missed deadlines.As political parties trade claims over who is responsible for the city's deteriorating air, residents continue to breathe the consequences. Ultimately, the success of any government's pollution plan will not be measured by the number of announcements or anti-smog guns deployed, but by whether Delhi can finally breathe easier, not just in winter, but throughout the year.The scale of the challenge, Dahiya said, cannot be understood by looking at Delhi's borders or the winter stubble-burning season alone.He said stubble burning accounts for less than 5% of Delhi's PM2.5 over a full year, while only around 30% of the city's pollution originates within its boundaries. This makes a regional approach essential, rather than one that focuses only on Delhi or relies on measures activated when AQI levels spike.He called for a regional airshed plan covering the NCR and the Indo-Gangetic plain, with year-round emission-reduction targets for vehicles, industries, power plants, waste, household fuel and dust. "We need targets for how many tonnes each source and each geography must cut, and by when," he said.Dr Mittal says the priority must be controlling pollution at its source through stricter checks on vehicular emissions, industrial pollution, construction dust and crop-residue burning."Clean air is a public health necessity, and controlling pollution at its source remains the most effective long-term solution," he says.So, until action moves beyond seasonal restrictions and visible interventions to measurable reductions in emissions, the capital risks returning to the same cycle of toxic air every winter.
Article Summary: Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) and Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) governments introduced separate action plans and announced a range of measures to tackle Delhi's recurring air pollution crisis. At the time of publishing this article on Saturday (7pm IST), Delhi's average Air Quality Index (AQI) stood at 367, in the ‘very poor’ category.

Article Title: After EASA concern, Air India asks crew to remain on board till replacement arrives during Europe fuelling halts
Article Text:
How Air India tackled the issues:

NEW DELHI: Air India has asked its cockpit and cabin crew operating flights between India and North America that take a fuelling halt in Europe since the US-Iran war broke out this Feb, to remain on board till the relief crew takes over from them to operate the remaining lag of the flight. The reason: Refuelling takes place during these halts which requires the cockpit to be manned by pilots and/or engineers for the process and since passengers remain on board during this time, cabin crew has to be there to announce precautions like keeping seat belts off.There were some instances when the incoming crew left the aircraft immediately on arrival in Europe. This gap in standard operating procedure (SOP) was detected primarily at Vienna during “EU ramp inspection programme” carried out to do “safety assessment of foreign aircraft” (SAFA). Along with cabin condition issues, this led to European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) SAFA score of Air India rising to 2.7, indicating safety-related deficiencies.The same was conveyed to the Indian Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA), which then swung into action along with AI to rectify the situation. The airline started deploying new or retrofitted aircraft on these routes which largely took care of cabin issues.For fuelling, AI asked its crew to remain on board till the replacement crew arrives.After taking these two steps, AI’s SAFA score has now gone to about 1.4, indicating that the issues that led to the earlier higher score have been largely addressed. “The DGCA did extensive monitoring and ensured AI followed the protocol to a T. Now AI is in the ‘good zone’ of Europe’s SAFA with the score falling from 2.7 earlier to about 1.4,” said people in the know. “Now crew often remains on board for about 1-1.5 hours after landing to oversee the fuelling process till relief crew arrives,” they add.AI’s improved SAFA score comes as a breather for the short-staffed DGCA that has been headed by non-aviation generalists for about two decades now, just ahead of facing an audit by the US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) from next week. It is also a relief for Air India as it is the only Indian carrier that flies to the US and will be examined closely by FAA for that reason. In operational terms, this should lead to less checks during fuelling stops in Europe and fewer delays on that count during halts there for AI.Refuelling: The SOP is that an engineering team and/or pilots should be in the flight deck when an aircraft is getting refuelled to coordinate with the fuelling staff. The cabin crew has to announce that passengers must not have their seat belts on when fuelling is taking place.The AI circular for pilots, reiterating the incoming set remains on board till it’s replaced by the relief crew. “Before commencing fuelling, the flight deck crew will be informed by engineering. If flight crew are unable to attend the flight deck during refueling, they shall request a qualified engineer to attend the flight deck,” says his circular.It adds: “NO PED (personal electronic devices) NO SMOKING / NO DEVICES / EXIT signs shall be illuminated as an indication to the cabin crew that fuelling is in progress. 'Seat belt' sign must be off. Known high energy equipment such as HF radios shall not be operated (during refuelling).”
Article Summary: Air India has asked its cockpit and cabin crew operating flights between India and North America to remain on board till the relief crew takes over from them. Refuelling takes place during these halts which requires the cockpit to be manned by pilots and/or engineers. The cabin crew has to announce that passengers must not have their seat belts on during fuelling.

Poll Vote & Share your view How effective do you believe the current government is in protecting those who expose corruption? Very effective Somewhat effective Not effective 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Highlighting that there is no protection for honest govt officials and also private persons who face the music for exposing corruption by suffering frequent transfers and non-consequential postings, Magsaysay award winner and IFS officer Sanjeev Chaturvedi has moved the Supreme Court for protection of whistleblowers, as the Centre has not notified the Whistleblower Protection Act despite it being passed by Parliament 12 years ago.The officer, who himself is fighting multiple service litigations, has pleaded the apex court to intervene to protect honest officers, as the Whistle Blowers Protection Act, 2014, has remained a dead letter. There is a "structural vacuum," and the "inaction of the Executive is not merely a policy failure - it is a constitutionally impermissible abdication of a statutory obligation that strikes at the foundational rights of whistleblowers as well as citizens. "Referring to the turbulence in his own career, particularly the alleged vindictive approach of the Congress govt of Haryana between 2008 and 2012, when he was transferred 12 times in four years and was suspended multiple times, he said, "Continuity of institutional persecution in the absence of any protective framework has become systemic norm.""The absence of the Act's operational framework means there is no single institutional mechanism to which a whistleblower in the petitioner's position can turn for protection, and there is no authority charged with the specific task of preventing and investigating retaliation," he said in an affidavit filed in SC."...The consequence of this executive inaction is that India has, for over 11 years, had no effective legislative framework for the protection of whistleblowers. During this period, countless potential disclosures of public corruption may have been suppressed, and brave individuals who did come forward have had no legal recourse."The affidavit said India, being a signatory to the United Nations Convention Against Corruption, is required to adopt appropriate measures to protect witnesses, experts, victims, and reporting persons from potential retaliation or intimidation, and that not doing so amounts to a governance deficit.
Article Summary: The officer, who himself is fighting multiple service litigations, has pleaded the apex court to intervene to protect honest officers. There is a "structural vacuum," and the "inaction of the Executive is not merely a policy failure," he says.

Article Title: Air purifier sales surge as pollution turns severe, demand spreads beyond metros
Article Text:
Gurugram: A vehicle-mounted anti-smog gun sprays water along a smog-shrouded road to mitigate air pollution, in Gurugram. (PTI Photo)(PTI11_15_2026_000089A)

Air purifier sales have surged across India as worsening air pollution drives consumer demand, with manufacturers and retailers reporting a sharp rise in enquiries and purchases, particularly after Diwali.The market, once largely limited to major metropolitan cities, is also expanding to other parts of the country, including Maharashtra, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Telangana, PTI reported. However, Delhi-NCR continued to dominate the segment, accounting for nearly 80 per cent of total sales volumes until 2025.Infiniti Retail, the Tata Group company that operates consumer electronics and durables chain Croma, said air purifier sales volumes had more than doubled in 2026."North India, particularly Delhi-NCR, remains the strongest market, while Mumbai also sees an uptick during periods of poor air quality," Infiniti Retail CEO and managing director Shibashish Roy told PTI.Roy said growing awareness of indoor air quality was encouraging more households to invest in air purifiers, although seasonal pollution remained a "key trigger" for demand.Online marketplace Amazon India also reported a significant increase in sales, saying purchases of air purifiers on its platform had doubled over the past week."Air purifier sales on Amazon have doubled in the last week," a company spokesperson told PTI. Article Title: India opposes UN call for death penalty moratorium, says no global consensus
Article Text:
"Travesty to term" capital punishment "state-inflicted death," said the India rep

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India voted against a United Nations General Assembly resolution calling for a global moratorium on the death penalty, maintaining that there is no international consensus against capital punishment and that sovereign states have the right to decide their own laws and penalties.The resolution, which called on countries to move towards abolishing the death penalty, was adopted by the UN General Assembly's Third Committee on Friday. India was among 33 countries that voted against it, while 133 supported the proposal and 16 abstained. The vote was in line with India's position in previous sessions, including in 2016, 2018 and 2024.India also opposed language in a separate resolution on extrajudicial, summary or arbitrary executions that linked the death penalty with torture and ill-treatment. While supporting the broader resolution, New Delhi disassociated itself from one of its paragraphs, arguing that lawful capital punishment following due process should not be equated with unlawful killings.Speaking at the committee, Bhavika Mangalanandan, first secretary at India's Permanent Mission to the UN, said capital punishment was permitted under international law, subject to restrictions."There is no international consensus against capital punishment, and article six of the ICCPR permits its use with restrictions.Capital punishment is meted out after rigorous and due legal process," she said, as quoted by ANI."It is therefore a travesty to term it state-inflicted death," she added.Mangalanandan objected to discussing capital punishment under a resolution dealing with extrajudicial and arbitrary executions, calling the approach "disingenuous and mischievous". She said it sought to present "personal ideological preferences as settled international law".India's objection was specifically to Operational Paragraph 6 of the resolution, which referred to recommendations made by the UN Special Rapporteur on extrajudicial, summary or arbitrary executions. The paragraph called on states to take those recommendations into account."We strongly disagree with the assertion conveyed in the report of the Special Rapporteur and thereby through the resolution. The death penalty inherently constitutes torture or ill-treatment," Mangalanandan said.Explaining India's position, she said the death penalty was a statutory provision in the country and was imposed only in the "rarest of rare" cases. She also cited procedural safeguards, including the presumption of innocence, mandatory confirmation of death sentences by a higher court and consideration of mitigating circumstances."Extrajudicial, summary or arbitrary executions are unlawful and a clear violation of human rights," she said, adding that India supported the broader resolution seeking to eradicate such violations.The United States also voted against the death penalty moratorium resolution, saying its language was problematic and that decisions on capital punishment should be left to individual countries' domestic democratic processes, subject to international law.US deputy representative to the UN Economic and Social Council Yaryna Ferencevych said Washington did not consider the lawful use of capital punishment inconsistent with respect for human rights. She also stressed that countries retaining the penalty must ensure fair trials and prohibit execution methods designed to cause undue pain or suffering.France, meanwhile, welcomed the resolution's adoption, describing it as an important step towards the universal abolition of the death penalty.
Article Summary: India voted against a resolution calling for a global moratorium on the death penalty. The resolution was adopted by the UN General Assembly's Third Committee on Friday. New Delhi disassociated itself from one of its paragraphs, arguing that lawful capital punishment following due process should not be equated with unlawful killings.

NEW DELHI: With mountain ecosystems facing growing climate threats, scientific evidence must guide policy decisions on mitigation and adaptation, particularly in the Himalayas, Pema Gyamtsho, Director General of the International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (ICIMOD).Speaking to PTI on the sidelines of the UN Climate Change Conference (COP31), Gyamtsho said scientific research must not remain confined to academic discussions but should translate into policies and decisions that address the impact of climate change on mountain regions.“Science needs to be followed in order to reduce the impacts of climate change on the mountains through mitigation and adaptation,” he said.He added that communicating scientific findings in a language understood by policymakers, local communities and climate negotiators was equally important.“In many cases, it's a question of the right kind of communication. However, science not being taken seriously is no excuse for us not to pursue this line because science has to inform policies. Ultimately, science has to inform the decisions that we make,” Gyamtsho said.On whether the Himalayas would feature in the final outcome of COP31, Gyamtsho said discussions at the conference indicated growing international attention to the region, particularly after recent disasters in Nepal.“From what I've heard at these different sessions, there's a lot of talk and attention on the Himalayas, particularly in connection with the recent disasters in Nepal,” he said.The conference, which began on November 9, saw proposals by Nepal, Bhutan and Kyrgyzstan to secure dedicated agenda space for mountain-related climate concerns fail to find support from major negotiating blocs.Nepal and Bhutan had sought a scientific assessment of mountain ecosystems, an annual high-level political dialogue and a dedicated UN climate work programme. They also called for mountain-specific priorities to be included in global climate adaptation and finance frameworks.Kyrgyzstan separately proposed an annual dialogue on mountains and climate change as a standing agenda item at meetings of the UN climate body's subsidiary bodies.Both proposals featured in the supplementary provisional agenda issued by the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) on November 6. However, neither was retained as a separate agenda item when countries adopted the agenda on the opening day.As a compromise, parties agreed that the COP31 presidency would hold consultations on mountain-related issues. Article Title: PUC tests to go tamper-proof, readings sent directly to central server; Delhi-NCR to be first
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Emission test results from vehicles tested at PUC centres in Delhi and adjoining cities in NCR can soon no longer be manipulated, with govt introducing stringent standards to ensure that actual pollution levels are recorded. The emission readings will be digitally signed and transmitted directly to the central server for enforcement purposes.The upgraded PUC equipment (gas analyser and smoke meter), compliant with the new standards, will first be rolled out in Delhi-NCR, followed by entire NCR, cities covered under National Clean Air Programme and, eventually, the rest of the country in a phased manner. The test run has started at a few PUC centres in Delhi, officials said.Officials said the phased deployment of PUC testing equipment complying with modified standard won’t have any impact on the acceptability of PUC certificates issued by other states and from centres that will take time to either get new equipment or upgrade them. They added that the nation-wide roll out is expected in the next two years.Under the amended automotive standards (AIS) published by road transport ministry, emission readings recorded by PUC equipment will have to be digitally signed within the instrument itself before being transmitted to the central Pollution Under Control Certificate (PUCC) server.The equipment will use a dedicated cellular connection to send the data, leaving no scope for operators or computer systems at testing centres to manually enter, modify or override measured emission values.The amended standards lay down detailed technical specifications and testing procedures for petrol and diesel emission-testing equipment, including gas analysers and smoke meters. A key feature is the installation of a specialised hardware security chip -- Trusted Platform Module (TPM 2.0) -- in each instrument. The chip will generate and securely store a unique private key that cannot be extracted or copied. Every emission test result will be digitally signed using this key, establishing the authenticity of the readings and the identity of the equipment that generated them.The instrument will transmit the signed data directly to the central server through its own SIM or eSIM connection. The computer at the PUC centre will be restricted to entering vehicle details, initiating the test and printing the certificate. It will not be able to alter the actual emission readings.Any unauthorised opening of equipment, attempts to modify its software, manipulation through external commands or unauthorised removal of its SIM will trigger an alert and suspend further testing and signing until the instrument is verified. Live emission readings will not be displayed during the test, preventing operators from influencing the outcome. If oxygen concentration is 5% or higher, the test will be aborted and a retest sought.
Article Summary: Emission test results from vehicles tested at PUC centres in Delhi and adjoining cities in NCR can soon no longer be manipulated. The emission readings will be digitally signed and transmitted directly to the central server for enforcement purposes. The upgraded PUC equipment (gas analyser and smoke meter), compliant with the new standards, will first be rolled out in Delhi-NCR.

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. He also held some of the newborns and presented the rings to beneficiaries during the launch programme.Under the scheme, eligible babies born in government hospitals and government primary health centres will receive a 22-carat, one-gram gold ring.The initiative, named the Maternal Uncle Gold Ring Scheme (Thaaimaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam), has an annual allocation of Rs 755.83 crore.It is aimed at celebrating motherhood, promoting maternal and child health and encouraging institutional deliveries by increasing public confidence in government healthcare facilities.The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions.Mothers must be registered under the Pregnancy and Infant Cohort Monitoring and Evaluation (PICME) system and have a Reproductive and Child Health (RCH) ID. They will also have to provide an e-KYC-verified Aadhaar card along with one of the prescribed identity or residence documents.These include ration cards, voter identity cards, Labour Welfare Board identity cards, Department of Posts address cards and nativity certificates.The state government has already procured 1.28 lakh one-gram gold rings for the initial rollout. Each ring will have a unique serial number and will be packed in tamper-proof packaging.From Monday, babies born in government hospitals will receive the rings at the time of discharge, according to the state government.To clear the backlog of eligible babies born between June 22 and Monday, the government will distribute the rings through 107 hubs across Tamil Nadu.Distribution will begin at the rate of 100 babies per day at each hub. At designated centres, 25 beneficiaries will be accommodated in the morning and another 25 in the afternoon to avoid overcrowding, PTI reported.Village Health Nurses will distribute invitations informing beneficiaries of their allotted date and time. Beneficiaries have been asked to visit the designated centres only at the time mentioned in their invitations.The district administration has also made transportation arrangements for beneficiaries from their respective areas. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election as a symbolic gift to newborns, drawing on the Tamil tradition of ‘Thaimaaman Seer’. The scheme has retrospective effect from June 22, Vijay’s birthday.A government order issued on June 23 described the initiative as a token celebrating the birth of a child, motherhood and the cultural tradition of ‘Thaimaaman’.According to ANI, Tamil Nadu minister Arun Raj explained the cultural significance of the initiative saying, "A maternal uncle is someone who is among the first to rush in when a child is born, sharing in his sister’s happiness as his own. He assures her that he will always stand by her and her child, offering love, support and a sense of security.""Today, the Tamil Nadu Government, under the leadership of our brother, Mr. Vijay, is embracing this sacred bond of the maternal uncle and, as a gesture of that affection, is set to provide a one-gram gold ring to every child born in government hospitals. When the scheme was announced and the question arose as to where it should be launched, the place chosen by our Chief Minister was Madurai. This is the sacred soil of Madurai, blessed with the compassion and grace of Mother Meenakshi," he added.Tamil Nadu records around 7.8 lakh deliveries annually, with institutional deliveries accounting for 99.9% of births, according to NFHS-6. Government health facilities account for nearly 4.2 lakh deliveries, or around 53% of the total.According to the state government, the average out-of-pocket expenditure for a delivery at a government hospital is Rs 1,364, compared with Rs 63,473 at a private hospital.The government said the scheme is intended to encourage safe institutional deliveries, strengthen maternal and child welfare and increase public trust in government healthcare services.The Tamil Nadu Medical Services Corporation will procure the gold rings based on annual requirements, while a project and programme management unit will oversee implementation and monitoring.

NEW DELHI: Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta on Saturday said the garbage mountains at the city's landfill sites were steadily shrinking as she reviewed waste disposal work at Okhla and laid the foundation stone for new waste processing facilities at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola.Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years, with a large portion of the cleared area also being turned green.She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed."Today, at Okhla, we have processed almost all the legacy waste that was there before January 2025," Gupta said.Gupta said the government was working on two fronts: clearing the existing garbage mountains while ensuring that fresh waste generated every day did not accumulate into new landfill sites.According to news agency ANI, she said around 3,000-4,000 metric tonnes of fresh waste reaches the sites daily and is being processed round the clock."The garbage currently piled up here is essentially fresh waste generated after January 2025, and that too is being processed round the clock. So, we are fighting on two fronts: one is eliminating waste, and the other is ensuring that the 3,000 to 4,000 metric tons of fresh waste arriving daily is processed immediately, so that new garbage mountains are not formed for future generations," Gupta said.She said the government was working to reduce the existing garbage mountains to zero."People are seeing that the garbage mountains are continuously shrinking and soon a time will come when they will become zero," Gupta said.Gupta also said she had taken what she described as her "last selfie" with the garbage mountain at Okhla."Today I have taken my last selfie with the garbage mountain; after this I have taken a pledge that this garbage mountain will end soon," she said.Taking a jibe at the Opposition, Gupta added, "I had said - garbage mountain, you will have to go; the opposition mocked. Today I will say the garbage mountain is going; now only its back remains."During the programme at the Okhla SLF site, Gupta laid the foundation stone for fresh waste processing plants at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola, as well as a biogas facility at Ghazipur. She also inaugurated the M&CW Centre at Kotla Mubarakpur through virtual mode from Okhla.The Okhla plant will be built at a cost of Rs 103 crore and will have a processing capacity of 1,400 metric tonnes per day.The Singhola facility will cost Rs 42 crore and have a capacity of 800 metric tonnes per day, while the Ghazipur plant will have a processing capacity of 700 metric tonnes per day.The facilities are intended to process fresh waste as well as construction and demolition waste. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure."Waste should not remain waste; Delhi should use it as wealth," she said, adding that new technologies were being introduced for waste segregation and processing.She said waste and cattle dung would be used to produce biogas and manure as part of efforts to build a technology-driven waste management system.Gupta said the government was taking up several measures to address pollution, including work on landfill waste, cleaning the Yamuna, dust mitigation, plantation, road infrastructure and waste management."Our government is tackling pollution from a 360-degree perspective to ensure it gradually decreases. We are working on every aspect, be it addressing the mountains of garbage, cleaning the Yamuna, improving road infrastructure, or managing waste, to ensure the people of Delhi enjoy better air quality. Our resolve and policies are absolutely clear, and we are working 24x7 in the public interest," she said.The chief minister also reviewed the progress of waste disposal work with officials and directed them to accelerate the work according to the stipulated timeline.She said the garbage mountains at Bhalswa, Ghazipur and Okhla had caused inconvenience to people travelling through these areas and said the government was continuing efforts to eliminate them.
Article Summary: Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years. She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure.

Article Title: India-US trade talks hit ‘plateau’: Sitharaman says further give-and-take ‘very, very difficult’
Article Text:
Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman

India stresses strategic autonomy in trade negotiations

India-EU pact opens market access

India and US have reached a “plateau” in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement, with further concessions from either side likely to be "very very difficult", finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman said on Monday. Speaking at the Munich Leaders Meeting in New Delhi, she said that while negotiations are still underway, any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side.“The agreement negotiations are still ongoing, although we'd like to believe that both the sides have reached a plateau beyond which giving or taking might be very, very difficult. But maybe if there are rooms to operate from, both sides would do it,” Sitharaman said.She said the agreement was still being “hard and very rigorously negotiated” and that India has a trade surplus with the US. “But what is the predominant feature of the trade relations between India and the US? The trade balance is very much in our favor.”Sitharaman said that the US would naturally want to reduce this trade imbalance and address what it sees as losses built up over the years.She also said that the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.“Negotiation used to be the only platform through which countries could highlight the discrepancies, highlight the lop-sidedness and say, would we want to correct this?” she said.“Tariff was an instrument of negotiation, and tariff had a certain framework within which you will apply it. Today framework is there, tariffs are going,” she said, while stressing that countries still need to negotiate and find “some give and take”.Sitharaman was also asked about maintaining strategic autonomy while negotiating bilateral trade agreements with European countries, including in the context of India procuring Russian oil."There is no Lindsay Graham Bill in Europe...," she said.On the broader question of how bilateral trade agreements can protect a country's interests in an era of multilateralism, Sitharaman said countries were increasingly choosing bilateral partnerships where they saw greater benefit.“Countries choose where multilateralism would benefit them, and there are some unique bilaterals which countries choose to have. The balance is somewhat tilted in favour of the bilateral rather than the multilateral,” she said.She said countries were now increasingly looking for new trade partners and strengthening those relationships through agreements.“Countries are now rapidly catching up with — I would put the EU-India also in a bilateral mode -because it's one in the name of union, but of course within them they have. So, bilaterals today are catching up far more than even initiating or beginning a multilateral. It's not deliberate, but in a way, if you don't do it, you're not moving forward. Countries will have to choose new partners for their trade and strengthen the tie through an agreement. And therefore, newer partnerships are being searched for, and they are tied up bilaterally.”FM Sitharaman cited the India-EU trade agreement as a major example of India's approach to negotiating trade pacts while protecting domestic interests.She said India had opened 92.5 per cent of its tariff lines and around 97 per cent of tariff value under the agreement. The EU, meanwhile, had opened 99 per cent in value terms and possibly 97 per cent of tariff lines.According to Sitharaman, greater access to the European market could support employment in labour-intensive sectors, including footwear, textiles, toys and processed products. Many of these sectors are linked to micro and small enterprises.“Those are all in the micro and small medium industry segment, which are labor-intensive,” Sitharaman said, adding that greater access to the European market could generate “more exports, more jobs”.Sitharaman said bilateral trade agreements were becoming increasingly important as multilateral institutions have weakened.“Multilateralism is not going to go away. But multilateralism has weakened,” she said.She also stressed that multilateralism should continue even as countries increasingly pursue bilateral agreements.“Multilateralism is not going to go away and multilateralism shouldn't go away,” Sitharaman said.The Munich Leaders Meeting, being held in the National Capital, provides a platform for about 100 senior decision-makers and experts to discuss opportunities for stronger cooperation among emerging and middle powers amid profound geopolitical change. Discussions include geoeconomic developments, trade and connectivity, maritime security, defence cooperation and other key international challenges.
Article Summary: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman says India and US have reached a 'plateau' in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement. She said any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side. She also said the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.

Article Title: Jio IPO sees bumper demand: India's largest public issue fully subscribed in just 100 minutes of opening
Article Text:
The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders.

Jio IPO

Jio IPO: Jio Platforms' $3.2 billion initial public offering (IPO) was fully subscribed within less than two hours of bidding opening on Wednesday, as investors rushed to participate in India's biggest-ever share sale. The offering is also the first IPO from billionaire Mukesh Ambani 's Reliance group in two decades.According to a PTI report, the Jio IPO was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of its opening on October 21.The rapid subscription was notable because large IPOs in India often see a slow start, with institutional investors typically placing their bids closer to the closing deadline. By comparison, the National Stock Exchange of India's share sale recently attracted subscriptions for just 42% of the shares on offer on its first day. Hyundai Motor India's IPO had received bids for only 18% of its offering on the opening day.Also Read | Jio IPO, India’s largest public issue, opens for subscription: Price band, GMP to brokerage views - top 10 things to know The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders. The issue will close on Friday, with shares priced in a band of Rs 1,065 to Rs 1,119 apiece.Exchange data showed that institutional investors had bid for 3.25 times the shares reserved for them by Wednesday. Retail participation was lower at that stage, with individual investors applying for 0.22 times their reserved quota.Retail investors have been allocated around one-third of the total offering.The IPO values Jio Platforms at as much as $108.3 billion. Once trading begins on October 28, the company could rank among India's largest listed companies by market capitalisation.Earlier this week, Jio Platforms allotted shares worth $853 million to domestic and international investors, including the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority and BlackRock. The anchor investor portion attracted bids exceeding $25 billion, according to a Reuters report.Backed by global investors such as Meta, Google's parent company Alphabet and other institutional investors, Jio Platforms houses India's largest telecom operator. With more than 500 million subscribers, the business is the world's second-largest telecom operator within a single country, behind China Mobile.This is Reliance's first IPO since 2006. Jio Platforms' telecom business, led by Ambani's son Akash, began operations in 2016. Its strategy was built around the expectation that Indians would use the internet much more extensively if access became almost free. By offering inexpensive data and free voice calls, Jio quickly gained market share from competitors such as Bharti Airtel and Vodafone Idea.
Article Summary: Jio IPO was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of its opening on October 21. The rapid subscription was notable because large IPOs in India often see a slow start. The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders. The issue will close on Friday, with shares priced in a band of Rs 1,065 to Rs1,119 apiece.

Article Title: LPG consumption down, diesel & petrol sales up in September
Article Text:
LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier

NEW DELHI: LPG demand fell by over 9% year-on-year in Sept, while petrol and diesel sales registered growth of 7% and 5%, respectively, provisional data released by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC) showed.LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier.Month-on-month consumption, however, registered a growth of 8%, up from 2.4 MT.Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT. Petrol and diesel consumption had registered year-on-year growth of 7.9% and 6.5%, respectively, in July.While petrol is largely used as an automobile fuel and its consumption is commensurate with the increasing number of vehicles, diesel is consumed by transport vehicles for passenger and freight movement, besides being used in the agricultural sector.Erratic monsoon conditions due to El Nino boosted demand for diesel for irrigation.Cumulative petrol consumption during Apr-Sept in the current financial year increased 7% to 22.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose 4.8% to 47.9 MT. In contrast, LPG consumption declined 14.9% to 13.8 MT from 16.2 MT during the corresponding period of 2025-26.
Article Summary: LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier. Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT.

Article Title: Gurgaon woman pays Rs 4,811 for dinner, restaurant refuses to remove Rs 401 service charge despite objection; consumer commission says mandatory service charge violates CCPA rules, orders refund and R

GURGAON: A dinner outing with friends in Gurgaon ended in a consumer dispute after a woman was charged an additional 10% service fee despite asking the restaurant to remove it. The Gurugram District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has directed the restaurant to pay her Rs 31,000, including compensation for mental harassment and litigation expenses. It has also ordered a refund of the Rs 401 service charge.The dispute dates back to May 16, 2026, when the woman visited the restaurant with her friends for dinner. She alleged that the bill included a service charge of Rs 401, equivalent to 10% of the amount. She objected to the additional charge and asked the restaurant to remove it. However, the establishment allegedly refused, leaving her with no option but to pay the entire bill of Rs 4,811, including the disputed fee.The woman later approached the consumer commission, arguing that the restaurant had violated the Central Consumer Protection Authority's (CCPA) guidelines on service charges. The restaurant did not appear before the commission despite being given an opportunity to respond. The proceedings were therefore conducted ex parte.In its order, the commission referred to the CCPA's guidelines issued on July 4, 2022, which prohibit hotels and restaurants from automatically adding a service charge to bills.The guidelines state that establishments cannot collect such charges by default or under another name. They also make clear that payment of a service charge must remain voluntary, with consumers free to decide whether they want to pay it.The commission said the restaurant had disregarded these provisions by refusing to remove the charge despite the customer's objection. It held the establishment guilty of deficiency in service and adopting an unfair trade practice, observing that its actions amounted to a blatant violation of the CCPA guidelines. Apart from ordering the restaurant to return the Rs 401 collected as service charge, the commission awarded the woman Rs 20,000 as compensation for mental harassment, pain and agony, and financial loss. It also directed the restaurant to pay Rs 11,000 towards litigation expenses, taking the total amount payable to Rs 31,401, including the refund.
Article Summary: A woman was charged an additional 10% service fee despite asking the restaurant to remove it. The Gurugram District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has ordered the establishment to pay her Rs 31,000. The commission awarded the woman Rs 20,000 as compensation for mental harassment, pain and agony, and financial loss.

Article Title: 'Preferential trade access already agreed': Piyush Goyal's big update on India-US trade deal
Article Text:
Union commerce minister Piyush Goyal

NEW DELHI: India has secured an agreement with the United States to receive preferential market access for its goods, with lower import duties than competing countries, commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal said on Sunday.Goyal said the understanding was reached between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and US President Donald Trump when the two countries announced a broad framework for their bilateral trade agreement (BTA). Negotiations are currently underway to finalise the first phase of the deal."This was already agreed between the leaders - President (Donald) Trump and Prime Minister Narendra Modi when they announced that we have both come to a broad framework agreement a few months ago and it has been acknowledged that India will get preferential trade access in the US with lower duties than our competitor countries," Goyal told reporters in Cairo.The minister is on a two-day visit to Egypt to discuss ways to strengthen trade and investment ties between the two countries.India and the US finalised the framework for the first phase of their bilateral trade agreement in February. The deal was expected to be signed earlier, but changes in the US tariff structure have led to further negotiations.An official had recently said that Washington had assured New Delhi of a comparative tariff advantage for Indian goods under the proposed agreement.Both sides are working to conclude the first tranche by the end of the current financial year."We will have to see how the tariff framework unfolds. We are working towards closing the first tranche by the end of this financial year. Talks are going for the first tranche and the broader BTA," the official said last week.The extent of the tariff advantage for Indian goods will depend on the final framework agreed upon by the two countries.The negotiations have also been affected by changes in US trade policy after the Supreme Court struck down President Trump's reciprocal tariffs, which had formed the basis of the earlier discussions. Washington is now exploring alternative mechanisms under provisions of the Trade Act to put a new tariff framework in place.
Article Summary: India and the US finalised the framework for the first phase of their bilateral trade agreement in February. The deal was expected to be signed earlier, but changes in the US tariff structure have led to further negotiations. Both sides are working to conclude the first tranche by the end of the current financial year.

Article Title: Mumbai man pays Rs 1.47 lakh to book flat in Poddar Riviera Phase-I, seeks cancellation after bank rejects home loan; builder fails to refund despite legal notice, consumer commission orders full repa

AI Generated Image Used For Representational Purpose Only

MUMBAI: The Additional District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Mumbai Suburban, held that a general non-refundable clause in a flat booking form cannot by itself justify retaining a buyer’s money when the developer fails to prove actual loss or a valid basis for forfeiture. This ruling was recently made by a Mumbai Suburban District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission ordering a builder to refund a buyer's booking deposit alongside interest, compensation for mental agony, and litigation costs, bringing the total financial liability to Rs 2.35 lakh. The commission, comprising President Pradeep G Kadu and Member Gauri M Kapse, directed Poddar Riviera Phase, Kalyan, to refund Rs 1.47 lakh to complainant Shyamsunder Madanlal Varma, who had booked a flat in the project but sought cancellation after banks did not sanction a housing loan.Varma had paid Rs 1.47 lakh towards booking of a flat in Poddar Riviera Phase-I at Mharal Village near Shahad Station. After the loan was not sanctioned, Varma requested cancellation and refund. Varma said repeated phone calls and emails did not result in repayment, and a legal notice dated Feb 17, 2022 also failed to secure a refund.The opposite party did not appear before the Commission despite service of notice, and the matter proceeded ex parte.The Commission relied on the payment receipts, legal notice and email correspondence placed on record by Varma.In the order authored by the commission noted, “The booking form contains a general stipulation that the booking amount and other charges would be non-refundable. The email correspondence dated Dec 23, 2021 and Dec 27, 2021 is significant. The opposite party itself agreed to refund the amount paid by the Complainant after deducting Rs.25,000.”The Commission found that Poddar Riviera Phase had not justified the proposed deduction. The order stated, “However, the Opposite Party has failed to establish any specific contractual terms and conditions justifying the forfeiture of Rs 25,000 in the circumstances of the present case.”The Commission further recorded, “There is no evidence on record to establish that the Opposite Party suffered any actual loss or that the proposed forfeiture of Rs 25,000 was justified. The mere existence of a general non-refundable clause does not, in the facts of the present case, sufficiently justify retention of the Complainant's money, particularly when the Opposite Party itself agreed to refund the amount after deduction.Holding the conduct to be deficiency in service, the Commission said, “Therefore, the Opposite Party has failed to justify the retention of the Complainant's amount. Their failure to refund the amount despite the Complainant's request amounts to deficiency in service.”The Commission awarded Rs 1.47 lakh as refund, Rs 20,000 as compensation for mental agony and harassment, and Rs 10,000 as litigation costs, making the total immediate award Rs 1.77 lakh. The order directed compliance within 45 days, failing which Poddar Riviera Phase must pay 9 percent annual interest on Rs 1.47 lakh l from June 1, 2022 until actual payment. If interest is calculated up to the order date, the interest is about Rs 58,351, taking the total liability to about Rs 2.35 lakh, with interest continuing until payment in case of default.
Article Summary: Mumbai Suburban District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission orders builder to refund a buyer's booking deposit alongside interest, compensation for mental agony, and litigation costs. The commission, comprising President Pradeep G Kadu and Member Gauri M Kapse, directed Poddar Riviera Phase, Kalyan, to refund Rs 1.47 lakh to complainant Shyamsunder Madanlal Varma.

Article Title: Liquor is Noida's problem; in Gurgaon and Delhi, it's obesity
Article Text:
Alcohol consumption also rose from 17.3% to 21.8%, marking the highest spikes among NCR cities (Representative image)

Tobacco use among men aged 15 and above in Noida increased significantly from 29.7% to 38.7%.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines





Nearly four in every 10 men aged 15 and above in Noida use tobacco, the highest among four NCR cities, including Delhi, Gurgaon and Ghaziabad, the latest National Family Health Survey (NFHS-6) has found.According to NFHS-6 (2023-24), tobacco use among men in Noida increased from 29.7% in NFHS-5 (2019-21) to 38.7%, a jump of nine percentage points. Noida also recorded a rise in alcohol consumption from 17.3% to 21.8%, the sharpest increase among the four cities, in the corresponding period.In Ghaziabad, tobacco use among men rose from 22.3% to 28.4% and alcohol consumption from 13.4% to 16.9% during the period.In contrast, Delhi saw a decline in tobacco use among men during the period from 26.2% to 21.3%. Alcohol consumption also went down from 21.6% to 16.1%. Gurgaon also recorded a substantial decline in tobacco use, from 32.6% to 23.7%, although alcohol consumption increased marginally from 18.5% to 19.9%.The survey revealed that the number of women consuming tobacco in Ghaziabad nearly doubled from 1.7% to 3.3% in the three years.The numbers fell in all three other cities - Noida recorded a decline from 3% to 2.3%, Gurgaon from 2.9% to 2.3%, and Delhi from 2.2% to 1.7%.Gurgaon recorded a sharp 17.6 percentage-point jump in overweight and obesity among women. The data show that the number of women in the 15 to 49 years age bracket with a body mass index (BMI) of 25 or above went up from 24.3% to 41.9% during the period. Delhi also recorded a marginal increase, from 41.4% to 42.7%.In contrast, Noida and Ghaziabad recorded declines in overweight and obesity among women. In Noida, the number of women with obesity fell from 34.7% to 30.2%, and in Ghaziabad it came down to 38.7% from 43.7%.However, the decline in overweight and obesity numbers was accompanied by an increase in underweight prevalence among women in all four cities. In Ghaziabad, the proportion of women with a BMI below 18.5 rose from 11.1% to 16%, while Noida recorded a marginal increase from 15% to 16%. Gurgaon also recorded a rise in underweight women, from 9% to 14.1%, while Delhi's figure increased from 10% to 12.4%.A BMI of 18.5-24.9 kg/m² is considered normal or healthy. A BMI below 18.5 is classified as underweight, 25-29.9 as overweight, and 30 or above as obese.The report also revealed contrasting trends in diabetes management across NCR. In Delhi, the number of men aged 15 and above with high or very high random blood sugar levels, or taking medication to control blood sugar, increased sharply from 14.1% to 22.2%. Among women, it rose from 12.2% to 19%.Ghaziabad recorded a sharper incidence among women, from 17.9% to 21.6%, compared with an increase from 20.2% to 20.8% among men. In Gurgaon, the proportion of men with high or very high random blood sugar levels, or taking medication to control blood sugar spikes, rose from 15.4% to 17.2%, while that among women dipped marginally from 13.5% to 13%.Noida was the only city where the high blood sugar indicators declined for both sexes. The prevalence among men fell from 17.2% to 13.6%, while among women it declined from 14.8% to 12.3%.The indicator includes adults with random blood sugar above 140 mg/dl or those taking medication to control it, and does not necessarily represent confirmed diabetes diagnoses.
Article Summary: Tobacco use among men aged 15 and above in Noida increased from 29.7% to 38.7%. Alcohol consumption also rose from 17.3% to 21.8%, marking the highest spikes among NCR cities. Gurgaon recorded a 17.6 percentage-point jump in overweight and obesity among women.

HYDERABAD: An irrigation department engineer was arrested after Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) raids across Telangana unearthed assets allegedly worth more than ₹25 crore, including a luxury villa, farmland, multiple plots, gold and investments, in a disproportionate assets case.The ACB’s central investigation unit registered a disproportionate assets case against R Satyanarayana (44), deputy executive engineer in the irrigation and command area development department, Nagarkurnool district, under the Prevention of Corruption Act and carried out simultaneous searches at 10 locations on Thursday.The raids covered Satyanarayana’s residence in Karmanghat, his office in Nagarkurnool, and properties linked to his relatives, family members and alleged benamis in Hyderabad, Wanaparthy and Nagarkurnool.Satyanarayana was at his native village, Shapur in Ghanpur mandal of Wanaparthy district, when the searches began.
