Article Title: Rupee extends winning streak, breaks below 94 against dollar: What's next
Article Text:
Rupee moves below 94 against US dollar

Crude oil prices cool as hopes of peace grow

Foreign fund inflows add to rupee's support

NEW DELHI: Rupee extended its gains for a second straight session on Monday, moving below the 94-per-dollar mark. The rally was supported by softer crude oil prices, stronger foreign fund inflows and hopes of easing tensions in the Middle East.The currency rose 24 paise to 93.74 against the US dollar in early trade. It opened at around 93.85 in the interbank forex market before gaining further. Rupee had already made a strong recovery on Friday, rising 43 paise to close at 93.98 against the greenback.Forex traders said rupee could maintain its positive momentum if diplomatic efforts in the Middle East make progress. Any easing of tensions could reduce the risk premium in crude oil prices, providing further support to the currency.These hopes gained ground over the weekend after US President Donald Trump indicated that further military strikes against Iran were highly unlikely if negotiations progressed and both sides reached a strong agreement.The easing in crude oil prices has been one of the key factors supporting rupee. Brent crude, which had earlier climbed to around $117.64, has now slipped below $100 and is trading near $98. Amit Pabari, managing director of CR Forex Advisors, said improving diplomatic expectations were already having an impact on energy prices."The improvement in diplomatic expectations is already reflecting in energy prices. Brent crude, which had climbed to around $117.64, has now slipped below $100 and is trading near $98. For currency markets, even the possibility of a lasting agreement is important," Pabari said.Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, was trading 0.15% lower at $98.17 per barrel in futures trade. The dollar index, which measures the greenback's strength against a basket of six currencies, was also down 0.12% at 102.18.Foreign investment activity provided another source of support for the domestic currency. Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) purchased equities worth Rs 13,749.82 crore on Friday, according to exchange data.The combination of lower crude prices and stronger foreign fund inflows has supported the rupee's recent gains against the dollar.With rupee now below the 94-per-dollar level, Pabari sees further room for appreciation. He expects the currency to move towards 93.50 and 93.00, while identifying 94.40–94.50 as the immediate resistance zone."With USD/INR breaking below the 94.00 mark, the probability of further rupee appreciation towards 93.50 and 93.00 has increased. On the upside, 94.40–94.50 is likely to act as the immediate resistance zone," Pabari said.Meanwhile, domestic equity markets opened lower on Monday. BSE Sensex fell 93.95 points to 80,919.19, while NSE Nifty declined 30 points to 24,968.80.Separately, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) reported that India's foreign exchange reserves declined by $2.691 billion to $717.056 billion in the week ended October 30.
Article Summary: Rupee extended its gains for a second straight session on Monday, moving below the 94-per-dollar mark. The rally was supported by softer crude oil prices, stronger foreign fund inflows and hopes of easing tensions in the Middle East. Rupee had already made a strong recovery on Friday, rising 43 paise to close at 93.98.

Article Title: Colette Kress sends her first email to employees as Nvidia interim CEO after Jensen Huang’s resignation: More than anything, I believe in...
Article Text:
Colette Kress, Nvidia’s CFO and now interim CEO, wrote to employees a day after Jensen Huang’s resignation.

Colette Kress will run Nvidia while keeping her CFO job

Nvidia earnings and an all-hands meeting land in Kress' first week

Here is Colette Kress' full email to Nvidia employees

Subject: RE: Statement from NVIDIA Board Chair

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Dear NVIDIAns,

I believe deeply in this company and in its future. More than anything, I believe in each of you, in our customers and partners and in the vital role we play every day in the global economy.

The Board, Estaff and I recognize that this has been an extraordinarily difficult period and I want you to know how grateful we are for your resilience, professionalism and continued dedication.

Thank you.

This company has achieved so much because of the work that all of you bring to it every single day. You are our greatest strength. You will hear more from leadership in the coming days about our future together, and we will host a company meeting on November 18 at 9am PT.

We play a vital role in building the technology that is powering the AI revolution, and we have important work ahead of us. So let's move forward together, with the same determination and commitment that have always defined this company.

Thank you for all you do,

Colette

Colette Kress has sent her first email to Nvidia employees as interim CEO, a day after Jensen Huang quit the company he co-founded 33 years ago. In the email, Kress tells staff that "more than anything" she believes in them. She thanks them for their "resilience, professionalism and continued dedication", and confirms a company-wide meeting on November 18 at 9am PT (10:30pm IST).The email comes at the end of a turbulent week. Nvidia's board put out statements on November 8 and November 10. Then on Thursday, Huang resigned as president, CEO and board member, effective immediately. He left after reports of extramarital affairs, including one with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. Kress sent the email as a reply to the new board chair's statement, and it does not mention Huang by name.Kress has been Nvidia's chief financial officer since September 2013. She will hold both roles until the board names a permanent CEO. Before Nvidia, she spent nearly 25 years in finance roles at Cisco and Microsoft. Investors know her voice well, as she has sat alongside Huang on the company's earnings calls for years.The board has also appointed Harvey C. Jones as Nvidia's first-ever chair. Jones is the former CEO and executive chairman of chip design software firm Synopsys. He said the board has "full confidence" in Kress and expects operations, customer commitments and the product roadmap to continue "without interruption". The search for a permanent CEO will consider internal and external candidates.Kress will not get a quiet start. Nvidia reports its third-quarter fiscal 2027 results on Tuesday, November 17, with the earnings call at 2pm PT. The employee meeting follows the next morning, US time.Markets have reacted. Nvidia shares opened down more than 13% after the resignation, wiping more than half a trillion dollars off its market value. Bernstein's Stacy Rasgon halved the firm's price target, writing in a note, "We've had enough and prefer to watch from the sidelines."Analysts have named three possible permanent successors: co-founder Chris Malachowsky; Ian Buck, who runs Nvidia's high-performance computing business; and Arm CEO Rene Haas. Who gets the job is the board's call. Until then, Kress is asking employees to stay focused on the work and "move forward together".
Article Summary: Colette Kress has been Nvidia's CFO since September 2013. She will hold both roles until the board names a permanent CEO. In the email, Kress tells staff that "more than anything" she believes in them. She thanks them for their "resilience, professionalism and continued dedication"

Article Title: Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan buy 440-acre Irish estate for about $57 million, featuring a Gothic castle, 16,000-square-foot mansion, historic architecture and stunning River Blackwater views
Article Text:
Inside Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan’s 440-acre Irish estate and Gothic castle

Mark Zuckerberg’s Irish castle purchase price and previous owners

Why Mark Zuckerberg chose Ireland for his latest property purchase

Zuckerberg's property portfolio stretches across several US states

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Mark Zuckerberg’s growing property portfolio and interest in classical history

Disclaimer: This article is based on publicly available reports and property records. The Times of India has not independently verified the transaction details, property valuation or total purchase price of the estate.

A historic Irish estate has become the latest addition to Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan’s growing property portfolio. The Meta chief executive and his wife have purchased Strancally Castle, a sprawling 440-acre property in County Waterford, Ireland, featuring a Gothic-style mansion overlooking the River Blackwater. The acquisition brings a 19th-century residence, with a history stretching back nearly 200 years, into the family’s collection of homes. The sprawling estate also includes extensive grounds, offering the couple a substantial private retreat in the Irish countryside.As reported by the Irish Times, dated October 7, 2026, the purchase price was initially estimated at between €20 million and €30 million. However, Ireland's Property Price Register subsequently recorded a sale figure of €51.17 million for the property, covering the principal residence and up to one acre of land. The total expenditure on the full estate is understood to be higher. The acquisition adds a historic European landmark to the couple’s extensive real estate holdings and highlights the continued appeal of secluded luxury estates among wealthy buyers.Strancally Castle sits on an extensive stretch of land in County Waterford, with the main residence occupying around 16,000 square feet. Strancally Castle is a three-storey Gothic Revival mansion spanning approximately 16,000 square feet, set within a 440-acre estate overlooking the River Blackwater.Its position overlooking the River Blackwater gives the property a distinctive setting in the Irish countryside.The house has undergone renovation work over the past two decades, bringing changes to a building that dates back to around 1830. Its original construction was commissioned by John Keily, a former member of the British Parliament. Irish architects James and George Richard Pain were responsible for its design. The brothers also worked on several other historic buildings in Ireland, including castle residences.The scale of the estate extends well beyond the main house. Its extensive grounds and historic architecture distinguish it from a conventional luxury residential purchase.The purchase price was subsequently disclosed through Ireland's Property Price Register. According to the Irish Times, Zuckerberg and Chan paid €51,171,155 for Strancally Castle, with the sale recorded on August 17, 2026. The registered figure covers the principal residence and up to one acre of land, meaning the couple's total expenditure on the entire 440-acre estate would be considerably higher.The estate was previously owned by Michael Alen-Buckley, co-founder of investment management firm RAB Capital, and his wife, Giancarla Alen-Buckley. The couple expressed their happiness at the change in ownership in a statement to the Irish Times, saying, “We leave our home of 25 years fondly and are grateful for the opportunity we have been given to save and restore Strancally Castle ... We are delighted that Mark and his family intend to build on our stewardship by continuing to invest in maintaining and enhancing the property and grounds as their home in a sustainable manner . .. We wish them and their family much happiness in this unique and blessed place.”Zuckerberg's spokesperson Brian Baker also confirmed the purchase. He said, “Mark and his family look forward to caring for this historic home and visiting when traveling to Ireland, where Meta maintains its international headquarters.”The location has a connection to Zuckerberg's professional life as well as his family's property interests. Ireland is home to Meta's European headquarters, which the company established in the country in 2009. Its substantial Irish operations make the country a destination for Zuckerberg's business-related visits.The company, which operates Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, has maintained a substantial presence in Ireland for years. The castle is therefore expected to serve as a place for the family to stay when visiting the country rather than simply another overseas property.The purchase also places the couple among wealthy technology executives who have acquired substantial residential properties outside the United States. Their latest acquisition is considerably different from the modern homes and large residential compounds more commonly associated with Silicon Valley fortunes.Strancally Castle is far from the first major property purchase made by Zuckerberg and Chan. The couple have built up an extensive collection of residential properties, with holdings in California, Hawaii and other parts of the United States.In Palo Alto, California, Zuckerberg reportedly spent more than $110 million acquiring at least 11 properties in the affluent Crescent Park neighbourhood. The purchases attracted attention from local residents as several homes in the area became part of his wider property holdings.He also previously owned a San Francisco residence, which he sold in 2022 for $31 million. In Washington, DC, the Meta founder paid approximately $23 million in cash for a mansion spanning around 15,000 square feet.Hawaii is another important part of the family's real estate interests. Zuckerberg has invested in a large property there, while Lake Tahoe is home to another sizable compound associated with the technology executive. His interest in water sports has also been visible on social media, where he has shared footage of himself hydrofoiling.The Irish castle adds a different kind of property to this collection, bringing historic European architecture into a portfolio otherwise centred largely on American residential estates.Zuckerberg's interest in classical history has occasionally appeared in his personal life. He and Chan have given their daughters names associated with Roman history, reflecting an interest in the ancient world, as reported by Los Angeles Times.Strancally Castle, with its 19th-century origins and Gothic architecture, offers another connection to European history. Its previous owners have expressed their hope that the property will remain well maintained under the family's ownership.Zuckerberg, who leads Meta, had an estimated fortune of more than $200 billion, according to Bloomberg's Billionaires Index in November 2026. The acquisition of the Waterford estate adds another substantial property to the family's holdings.
Article Summary: Zuckerberg and his wife have purchased Strancally Castle, a sprawling 440-acre property in County Waterford, Ireland. The acquisition brings a 19th-century residence, with a history stretching back nearly 200 years, into the family’s collection of homes. Ireland is home to Meta's European headquarters, which the company established in the country in 2009.

Article Title: Factories shut as Bangladesh garment workers intensify protests over minimum wage
Article Text:
Garment workers are demanding a minimum monthly wage of 30,000 taka

What are the workers demanding?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Bangladesh was rocked by fresh labour unrest on Sunday, with 13 garment factories shutting indefinitely and five others declaring a one-day holiday as workers intensified protests demanding a sharp increase in the minimum wage. The disruption came a day before the government-appointed wage board was scheduled to meet to discuss a revised pay structure.Protesting workers gathered in Gazipur's Konabari and Mouchak areas, prompting police to use tear gas and sound grenades to disperse them. Factory owners said around 50 units across the industrial zone were closed, although production continued at most factories.The workers have been protesting for weeks, demanding an increase in their minimum monthly wage from 12,500 taka (around $100) to 30,000 taka (around $240)."Workers made attempts to gather at different locations this morning, but law enforcement personnel prevented them with their prompt actions and remain deployed at every key point in the industrial area," Gazipur Industrial Police Superintendent Amzad Hossain said.Authorities deployed 13 platoons of Border Guard Bangladesh personnel alongside police in riot gear and the elite Special Response Battalion to maintain order and protect factories.Twenty-five executive magistrates were also assigned to oversee security arrangements.Garment workers are demanding a minimum monthly wage of 30,000 taka, arguing that their current earnings are insufficient to meet rising expenses on food, housing, transport and healthcare. Their protests have centred on the demand for a "living wage to survive".The government formed a Minimum Wage Board on November 1 to recommend a revised pay structure. The board aims to finalise its recommendations by the end of November, with the new wages expected to take effect from December 1. Workers are expected to receive their first salaries under the revised structure in January.The Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA) said its representatives would attend Monday's meeting to submit their proposal, but warned that its participation in subsequent discussions would depend on the situation.The unrest has raised concerns over export disruptions during the peak production season for spring and summer orders. Factory owners have warned that prolonged shutdowns could delay shipments and lead to cancellations.Bangladesh is the world's second-largest garment exporter after China. The sector employs more than four million workers and accounts for over 80 per cent of the country's export earnings.
Article Summary: Bangladesh rocked by fresh labour unrest on Sunday. 13 garment factories shut indefinitely and five others declared a one-day holiday. The disruption came a day before the government-appointed wage board was scheduled to meet to discuss a revised pay structure. Workers are demanding a minimum monthly wage of 30,000 taka.

New Delhi: To facilitate the growing commuter demand on the Delhi–Meerut Namo Bharat corridor and save time during rush hours, National Capital Region Transport Corporation (NCRTC) is set to operate Fast Namo Bharat train services during peak morning and evening hours starting Monday.These new limited-stop services will cut commute times further and enable passengers to travel from Anand Vihar to Ghaziabad in just eight minutes, Ghaziabad to Begumpul in 28 minutes, and Anand Vihar to Begumpul in a 36 minutes, while covering the entire corridor in less than 50 minutes.In the morning peak hours, two fast trains will depart from both terminal stations, Sarai Kale Khan towards Modipuram and from Modipuram towards Sarai Kale Khan, at 8 am and 8.30 am. Similarly, during the evening peak hours, two fast trains will leave from both terminal stations at 6 pm and 6:30 pm in each direction. These fast trains are additional services introduced by NCRTC to the existing regular Namo Bharat trains, which operate every 10 minutes.“Regular Namo Bharat train services will continue to operate as usual alongside these fast trains. Commuters are advised to check station display boards and listen to platform announcements before boarding to confirm whether a train is a fast or regular service,” said an official of NCRTC, which is implementing the Delhi-Ghaziabad-Meerut RRTS project.To ensure rapid transit, these fast trains will stop at only five major stations along the corridor: Sarai Kale Khan, Anand Vihar, Ghaziabad, Begumpul, and Modipuram. “NCRTC values the time of its daily commuters, and this enhanced peak-hour connectivity is designed to shave critical minutes off daily journeys, making it especially beneficial for students and office-goers who rely on punctual, high-speed transit to reach their workplaces and educational institutions on time,” said the official.About 1.1 lakh commuters travel every day on the corridor, with consistent growth in daily footfall. The corridor recently crossed the milestone of five crore commuter journeys, and over the past three months alone, the system recorded an average monthly ridership of more than 32 lakh.
Article Summary: New limited-stop services will cut commute times further and enable passengers to travel from Anand Vihar to Ghaziabad in just eight minutes. These fast trains are additional services introduced by NCRTC to the existing regular Namo Bharat trains, which operate every 10 minutes.

Article Title: Maharashtra FDA seizes Rs 1.39 crore nutraceuticals containing rejected ingredients
Article Text:
The Maharashtra FDA seized health supplements valued at Rs 1.39 crore from various establishments statewide (Representative image)

MUMBAI: In a crackdown on health supplements containing ingredients rejected by the country’s food safety regulator, the Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) seized nutraceutical products worth Rs 1.39 crore from 17 establishments across the state.A major seizure was made at a warehouse in Bhiwandi in Thane district, where stock worth Rs 47.65 lakh was confiscated, one of the highest values seized at a single establishment during the drive.The statewide operation, conducted simultaneously on November 13, targeted manufacturers, marketers, distributors and sellers of health supplements and foods for special dietary use.FDA officials found products containing two ingredients, magnesium acetyl taurate and nicotinamide mononucleotide, whose product approval applications had been rejected by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI).The Bhiwandi seizure was made at Kanchan Pharma Pvt Ltd’s warehouse at Bhumi World Industrial Park, Pimplas. The company also figured in the crackdown at other locations, including Pune and Nagpur.Across the state, stock worth Rs 1.3 crore was seized from 17 establishments.Four products were identified in the FDA action: Rejuvance, Altibrain-S, Magladense and EQOQ.The formulations contained one or both of the ingredients flagged by FSSAI, along with other substances, said the FDA press release.According to the FDA, the action followed FSSAI directions issued on June 3, concerning the product approval applications for the two ingredients.Officials said manufacturers had made the products without obtaining the necessary approval, while marketers had sold them without including the relevant food category in their licences.The nutraceutical crackdown was part of a wider statewide food safety drive under the FDA’s ‘Safe Food, Safe Maharashtra’ campaign.The FDA also acted against seven establishments and vehicles involved in the storage and sale of prohibited products such as gutka and scented pan masala, seizing stock and a vehicle.In Mumbai, the FDA seized prohibited food articles worth Rs 31,149 from six pan shops in Dahisar, Dharavi, Goregaon and Antop Hill.
Article Summary: The Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) seized nutraceutical products worth Rs 1.39 crore from 17 establishments across the state. A major seizure was made at a warehouse in Bhiwandi in Thane district, where stock worth Rs 47.65 lakh was confiscated.

Article Title: Homes that fail to process waste may face 235 fee in Mumbai
Article Text:
Mumbai currently generates around 7,000 metric tonnes of solid waste daily, apart from a similar quantum of construction and demolition (C&D) waste.

bulk waste generators

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines





MUMBAI: BMC’s solid waste management department has proposed a charge of Rs 235 per household on residents of buildings classified as bulk waste generators (BWGs) that fail to process their solid waste on their premises.TOI was the first to report on Oct 15 that BMC was working on a proposal to charge individual residential flats in BWG buildings that do not have facilities to process wet waste on their premises; however, the amount was yet to be finalised.Officials, however, justifying the move, have said that the same is aimed at enforcing the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026, which place greater responsibility on bulk waste generators to manage and process the waste they produce.A BMC official said, “ These requirements are part of a nationwide regulatory framework and are being implemented under the Supreme Court’s continuing directions and monitoring. BMC’s proposed framework is intended to facilitate compliance rather than merely impose charges.”Mumbai currently generates around 7,000 metric tonnes of solid waste daily, apart from a similar quantum of construction and demolition (C&D) waste.Under the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026, premises are classified as bulk waste generators if they meet any one of three criteria: a floor area of at least 20,000 sq m, daily water consumption of at least 40,000 litres, or daily waste generation of at least 100 kg.Meeting even one of these thresholds is sufficient for a premises to qualify as a BWG. The proposed charge of Rs 235 per household has been calculated based on BMC’s expenditure on solid waste management, which currently stands at about Rs 3,500 per tonne.The charges will not be immediately levied but after a period of three months, during which the civic body plans to encourage bulk waste generators to undertake scientific processing of waste on their premises.Civic officials said that BWGs that undertake scientific processing of waste at their premises may receive a property tax rebate of up to 15%.“Where individual societies lack adequate space or infrastructure, neighbouring societies may come together, form a special purpose vehicle and establish a common BMC-approved processing facility.“Only qualifying residential BWGs that are unable to process wet waste, obtain exemption and hand over such waste to BMC for collection, transportation and scientific processing will come under the Extended Bulk Waste Generator Responsibility certificate mechanism.UBT Shiv Sena MLA Aaditya Thackeray said, “The BJP is only trying to squeeze the citizens at all levels.”
Article Summary: BMC’s solid waste management department has proposed a charge of Rs 235 per household on residents of buildings that fail to process their solid waste on their premises. Mumbai currently generates around 7,000 metric tonnes of solid waste daily, apart from a similar quantum of construction and demolition (C&D) waste.

Article Title: TMC tightens water monitoring amid prolonged scarcity in Thane
Article Text:

Facing criticism over its handling of the city’s water supply crisis, Thane Municipal Corporation (TMC) is turning to tighter monitoring to plug leakages, curb water theft and regulate distribution among others as it braces for prolonged scarcity amid the potential impact of El Niño.Municipal Commissioner Saurabh Rao recently reviewed the situation and directed officials to undertake micro-level planning for the next nine to ten months, with fortnightly action plans to be drawn up until June 2027.A key priority is identifying and disconnecting unauthorised water connections. Dedicated teams will be formed across ward committee areas to detect illegal connections, while cases will be registered against those involved in water theft. The functioning of valve operators responsible for regulating distribution will also come under scrutiny, officials said.The civic body is also exploring an online registration and record-management system for water tankers on the lines of Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC). All municipal tankers will undergo GPS mapping, while private tankers’ water sources, filling points and extraction practices will be closely monitored.In a bid to reserve potable water for essential needs, TMC plans to prohibit its use at vehicle washing stations, construction sites, gardens and other non-essential activities. Water supply to major infrastructure projects, including Metro, Elevated Corridor, Coastal Road and Ring Metro, has been suspended until further orders. These projects have been directed to use treated wastewater from sewage treatment plants instead.The corporation will also step up efforts to revive public wells as alternative water sources. Of the 350 public wells within its jurisdiction, 202 are considered suitable for use. While 35 have already been revived and are operational, the remaining wells will be cleaned, repaired and restored on priority, officials said.
Article Summary: Thane Municipal Corporation (TMC) is turning to tighter monitoring to plug leakages, curb water theft and regulate distribution. A key priority is identifying and disconnecting unauthorised water connections. Dedicated teams will be formed across ward committee areas to detect illegal connections.
